title: Repo, deploy pipeline, and Next.js scaffold

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL. Audited commit 04848fa, working tree clean, sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. All 8 requirements are met and were verified from real output, not from the handoff assertions. One demonstrated defect blocks.

REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE - all MET:
Req 1: .gitignore has node_modules/, .next/, .env* plus negation for .env.example, and all three original Fully Completely lines are preserved. git log --all --diff-filter=A across full history shows no node_modules or .next path was ever committed, not merely untracked after the fact.
Req 2: swept the full tracked tree. Only connection-string hits are the two placeholder lines in .env.example (user:password@host:5432/dbname). No tokens, keys or secret-shaped values anywhere tracked. git check-ignore confirms .env.local is ignored while .env.example is NOT ignored, so the negation ordering is correct. .env.local exists on disk and is untracked. .env.example names both variables lib/db.ts actually reads.
Req 3: App Router confirmed (app/ present, no pages/). TypeScript with strict true. npm run lint exit 0. npm run build exit 0. Both run by me, not taken on trust. eslint.config.mjs excludes scripts/, templates/ and .claude/ only - framework tooling that predates the app. App code in app/ and lib/ is still linted, so this is scoping, not suppression.
Req 4: lib/db.ts reads process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? process.env.POSTGRES_URL. Nothing hardcoded. Handoff states what was actually provisioned (Neon via Vercel marketplace, resource neon-alizarin-paddle) rather than restating the flagged assumption as fact, which is what this criterion asked for. Choosing pg over a vendor SDK matches the implementation-agnostic framing.
Req 5: real SELECT 1 AS ok round-trip. The 200 is unreachable except after the awaited query resolves AND the row value is checked; there is no early-return path to success. Timestamp is new Date().toISOString() inside the handler, not module scope.
Req 6: export const dynamic = force-dynamic is present with an accurate comment. Independently corroborated by build output, which lists /api/health as dynamic (server-rendered on demand), not static. Whether it holds live is LiveQA.
Req 7: traced the catch path. Response body is exactly status, timestamp, message: Service unavailable. The caught error object goes only to console.error. No connection string, host, credential or driver object reaches the body. Error is logged, never swallowed.
Req 8: no deploy config committed that could contradict auto-deploy from main; .vercel is ignored and no vercel.json exists. Nothing in the repo conflicts. Actual deploy behaviour is LiveQA.

BLOCKING ISSUE - high severity - lib/db.ts line 28
new Pool({ connectionString }) is constructed with zero error listeners. pg attaches its own idleListener to every client after connect (pg-pool/index.js line 62 and line 380), and that listener calls pool.emit(error, err, client). Pool extends EventEmitter, so an error emitted with no listener is an uncaught exception and the process dies.
Why this matters here: it fires on an IDLE client, between requests, so the try/catch in app/api/health/route.ts cannot catch it - no request is in flight. Instead of the designed 503 with a status field, the function instance dies and the platform returns a generic 500 with no JSON body at all. That directly undercuts the failure contract Req 5 and Req 7 specify.
Demonstrated, not argued. Repro used the projects own pg-pool install and pg-pools real idleListener path, with a stub Client injected via options.Client purely to control when the socket error fires: request 1 returns 200 normally, the now-idle client then emits ECONNRESET, and the process exits with an uncaught exception that never reaches the route try/catch. Falsification test: the identical script with a single pool.on(error) listener added logs the error and survives, exit 0. Zero listeners crashes, one listener does not. That isolates the cause to the missing handler.
Not exotic, given what was actually provisioned: Neon autosuspends idle compute by default and terminates its connections, and a warm Vercel instance holds pooled idle clients across invocations. pg-pool documents this exact event and instructs handling it the same way you would treat process.on(uncaughtException). The library requires this handler; the code omits it. Note honestly: the crash mechanism is confirmed, the production trigger frequency is high-likelihood but I did not prove it inside Vercel runtime, and this is not something LiveQA can reliably trigger either. That is a reason to fix it now, not a reason to defer it.

REQUIRED FIX - roughly three lines in lib/db.ts, attach an error handler to the pool at construction, log the error and let the pool discard the dead client. Do not swallow it silently and do not call process.exit in a serverless handler.

WHY THIS BLOCKS RATHER THAN SHIPS WITH A NOTE: lib/db.ts is the foundation sprints 2 and 3 both import, so this gets harder to change once it is load-bearing. More to the point, a health endpoint that crashes the server when the database goes away is worse than no health endpoint - it is actively misleading, and being a truthful database signal is the entire reason this sprint exists. The sprint file itself names looks finished while being broken as the risk it is built to prevent.

CODE QUALITY - otherwise good. Clean separation between the pool wrapper and the route. Comments explain why rather than what, and the module-scope pool versus per-request timestamp distinction is reasoned through correctly rather than stumbled into. No SQL injection surface (no user input, and query is parameterized by design). No shared types redefined locally. No tests, correctly - the sprint explicitly puts a test suite out of scope and there is no app logic yet to cover. Build artifacts and the stray Neon agent-skill files were correctly kept out of the commit. Non-blocking, for sprint 2 not now: app/layout.tsx still carries the default Create Next App metadata title.

PASS: PASS (round 2). Audited commit 1fdeb4c, working tree clean. Sprint file re-read and confirmed unchanged since round 1 - last touched at ca742f6, zero diff across 04848fa..HEAD - so round 1 requirement coverage stands unchanged and this re-audit focused on the fix, as intended for a small isolated change.

SCOPE OF THE FIX: git diff --stat 04848fa..HEAD shows exactly two files - lib/db.ts (+14) and docs/sprints/state/sprint-1.json (my own round 1 bookkeeping). No scope creep, nothing else touched, route.ts untouched.

THE ROUND 1 BLOCKER IS RESOLVED AND VERIFIED, not accepted on the diff. lib/db.ts now attaches pool.on(error) immediately after construction, inside the same if (!pool) guard, so it is attached exactly once and there is no async gap between construction and attachment during which an event could be missed. Handler logs via console.error and returns. No process.exit, no rethrow from the listener - both correct for a serverless handler, and both were explicit in the round 1 required fix.

VERIFICATION - A/B against the real module, not a synthetic emit. I compiled the actual lib/db.ts to CommonJS and drove it through pg-pools real idle-client path (real pg, real pg-pool, real makeIdleListener; only the leaf Client was stubbed, to control when the socket error fires, injected by subclassing the Pool the module itself constructs). Same harness, same input, only the module under test differs:
CONTROL, round 1 code at 04848fa: listeners 0, idle client takes an ECONNRESET, uncaught exception, instance dies.
FIXED, current code at 1fdeb4c: listeners 1, same ECONNRESET, error logged as [lib/db] idle client error, instance survives, exit 0.
That is a controlled A/B, not a before-only demonstration: the harness provably still catches the defect, so the pass is evidence the fix works rather than evidence the test went blind.

NO REGRESSION: npm run lint exit 0 and npm run build exit 0, both re-run by me. Build output still lists /api/health as dynamic (server-rendered on demand), not static, so Req 6 still holds after the change. Working tree clean.

REQUIREMENTS 1-8: all remain MET exactly as recorded in round 1 notes - the requirements file did not change and the only code delta is additive error handling in the pool constructor. Nothing in round 1 coverage needs restating or revisiting.

ON THE ACKNOWLEDGED LIMITATION: Dev Team correctly flagged again that the realistic trigger - Neon autosuspending a warm Vercel instances pooled idle connection - remains unobserved in the real runtime, rather than letting a clean re-audit imply it had been. That is the right call and it is exactly how I characterised it in round 1. It does not hold up this gate. The crash mechanism was confirmed, the fix is the documented pg remedy for that specific event, and the A/B above proves the remedy is actually wired into this module. LiveQA cannot reliably trigger this either, so it should not be treated as an open live-test item; it is closed on mechanism, which is the appropriate standard for a static gate.

CODE QUALITY: the fix is minimal and correctly placed. The comment explains why the listener is mandatory rather than restating what the line does, which is the right instinct. Still no automated tests, still correct - the sprint puts a test suite explicitly out of scope and sprint 2 introduces the first logic worth covering. Non-blocking, for sprint 2: app/layout.tsx still carries the default Create Next App metadata title.

CLEARED FOR /sprint-dev-done then Pipeman. LiveQA still owns the live criteria this audit cannot settle: the two-timestamp check, the deployed 200 proving Vercel runtime can actually reach Neon, and the Req 7 preview-deployment failure-path attempt.

FAIL: FAIL - live test round 1. Tested commit 19ffc3d directly (production deployment j62n8f0jw, built from "Cloning ... Branch: main, Commit: 19ffc3d"), plus every other production deployment and alias. Env: curl + Vercel CLI 59.23.2 against Vercel production, 2026-09-19 ~20:15-20:20 UTC.

BLOCKER 1 - The deployed app serves nothing. Every route 404s on every deployment and every alias.

Observed, root and /api/health, HTTP 404 on all five URLs:
  textbook-gear-swap-board.vercel.app (production alias)
  textbook-gear-swap-board-element-iq.vercel.app
  textbook-gear-swap-board-git-main-element-iq.vercel.app
  textbook-gear-swap-board-t4xrnnbps-element-iq.vercel.app (commit 111b8e2)
  textbook-gear-swap-board-j62n8f0jw-element-iq.vercel.app (commit 19ffc3d - THE SHIPPED COMMIT)
  textbook-gear-swap-board-n385w2lpb-element-iq.vercel.app (commit cd034da)

Verbatim body, content-type text/plain, identical at root and /api/health:
  "The page could not be found"
  "NOT_FOUND"
  "pdx1::65d8c-1789849111608-f1e2a3faf17e"

Not commit-specific: three separate commits (cd034da, 19ffc3d, 111b8e2) all 404 identically. This is project configuration, not code.

ROOT CAUSE, proven live, not inferred. Vercel project settings read:
  Framework Preset = "Other"   (should be Next.js)
  Output Directory = "public" if it exists, or "."
  Root Directory = "."
The build itself SUCCEEDS and emits the correct route table. Build log for the deployment of 111b8e2 shows:
  "Next.js 16.3.5 (Turbopack)"
  "Compiled successfully in 5.7s"
  Route (app):  "o /"  ,  "o /_not-found"  ,  "f /api/health"
  ("f" = Dynamic, server-rendered on demand - so the force-dynamic opt-out DID take effect at build time)
  "Build Completed in /vercel/output [13s]" / "Deployment completed"
Because the preset is "Other", Vercel discards the Next.js server output and serves the raw public/ directory as a static site.

PROOF that public/ is what is being served (this is the decisive check, not a theory):
  /file.svg   -> HTTP 200
  /globe.svg  -> HTTP 200
  /next.svg   -> HTTP 200
  /vercel.svg -> HTTP 200
  /window.svg -> HTTP 200
  (all five files that exist in public/, served at site root)
  /_next/static/chunks/main.js -> HTTP 404   (no Next.js output wired up at all)

Fix is in the Vercel project settings, not in the diff: set Framework Preset to Next.js (clear the Output Directory override), then redeploy. QA1 could not have caught this - Req 8's committed config is consistent with auto-deploy and there is no vercel.json to be wrong. Auto-deploy on push to main DOES work (three pushes produced three deployments); what is broken is how the output is served.

CRITERION-BY-CRITERION:
Reqs 4/5/8 - /api/health returns 200 with well-formed JSON: FAIL. Got HTTP 404, content-type text/plain, body "The page could not be found / NOT_FOUND". No JSON, no status field, no timestamp. The Postgres round-trip from Vercel's runtime - the entire point of this sprint - is therefore still UNPROVEN, neither confirmed nor refuted.

Req 6 - two requests several seconds apart return different timestamps: CANNOT RUN, blocked by Blocker 1. Attempted and recorded rather than skipped: request 1 at 20:18:31Z, request 2 at 20:19:15Z (44s apart). Both HTTP 404. Zero timestamp fields in either body (grep for timestamp/status/ok across both responses returned 0 matches). No timestamps exist to compare. Must be re-run after the fix - the build log's "f /api/health" is static evidence the opt-out compiled, but that is QA1's half of Req 6, and the live half is still unverified.

Req 3/8 - site root renders without a runtime or build error page: FAIL. Root returns HTTP 404 "The page could not be found". It is not a Next.js error page - it is a platform 404, because no app is being served.

Req 7 - failure path leaks no connection string, host, credential or stack trace: NOT TESTED, blocked, and explicitly not waived. What was attempted: the criterion's intended route is a preview deployment with a deliberately wrong DB variable. What blocked it: the health handler is unreachable on every deployed URL regardless of any environment variable, so its error path cannot be exercised at all - a preview deploy would 404 identically for the same preset reason, and pointing a variable at a bad host would change nothing about a 404 raised before any handler runs. This is blocked by Blocker 1 specifically, not by an unavailable environment, and I did not create a preview deployment because deploying is Pipeman's action, not LiveQA's. Re-test Req 7 once Blocker 1 is fixed; it remains outstanding and unverified.
  Partial, non-substitute observation: the platform 404 body itself leaks nothing (swept for postgres/neon/password/connection-string/stack-frame patterns - 0 matches). That is Vercel's 404, NOT the handler's failure path, and it does not satisfy Req 7.

NOTE FOR THE FIX LOOP: origin/main is at 111b8e2, two commits past the shipped 19ffc3d. Both intervening commits (d2d1520 ship bookkeeping, 111b8e2 .gitignore) touch zero application code - "git diff --name-only 19ffc3d 111b8e2 -- app lib package.json next.config.ts tsconfig.json" is empty - so testing the 19ffc3d deployment directly was valid and the newer deployment behaves identically.

Nothing here is a code defect I can point at. The diff appears to do what it claims; the project it deploys into is misconfigured. Dev Team/Pipeman fix the Vercel preset, redeploy, and I re-test all four criteria including Req 7.
